slides: Welcome back. Before the advanced questions, let's see what happens on the number line when we multiply by a negative number.

slides.say: Multiplying a nonzero number by a positive number keeps it on the same side of zero. Multiplying by a negative number moves it to the other side. For example, three times negative one is negative three. Seven times negative one is negative seven.
We multiplied both numbers by the same negative number. Three was smaller than seven, but negative three is larger than negative seven. So their order has reversed.
Let's check again. Two is smaller than five. Multiply both by negative two. We get negative four and negative ten. Negative four is larger than negative ten. Their order has reversed again.

This is why, when we multiply both sides of an inequality by a negative number, we reverse the inequality sign. Now we're ready for the advanced questions. Try each one before watching its explanation. Okay. I'll see you in the next video.
